title: Metric ghosts and alert backfill retrospective
content:
Summary:

This note covers the Feb 12–13 incident where a Prometheus ingestion backfill caused a ~3 hour pager storm (multiple teams) from apparent SLO burns and duplicate alerts. We observed spikes in error-rate and latency alerts that did not match live traffic or customer reports; investigation showed the source was late-arriving samples and stream replays from an upstream aggregator job, causing 'metric ghosts' (stale timestamps + high cardinality tags) and alert backfill.

Why this matters:
- Pager fatigue: >20 duplicated pages in 120 minutes, several oncall rotations interrupted.
- False SLO burns: cosmetics led to automated rollbacks and temporary traffic shifts in a canary.
- Cost & noise: increased alerting noise masked an unrelated real issue we missed for 17 minutes.

Incident timeline (high level):
- 2025-02-12 01:12 UTC — upstream extract job failed, buffering to S3.
- 2025-02-12 02:00–09:00 UTC — retries created multiple partial backfills (S3->ingest) with overlapping windows.
- 2025-02-13 00:45 UTC — ingestion consumer caught up and replayed ~14M samples with original timestamps.
- 2025-02-13 00:50 UTC — Grafana alert engine fired burst of latency/error rate alerts for 20 services.
- 2025-02-13 01:05 UTC — oncall SRE (Daniel) notes alerts don't correlate with customer tickets or APM traces.
- 2025-02-13 01:22 UTC — confirmed ingestion lag metric and ingestion consumer restart trace backfill.
- 2025-02-13 01:40 UTC — implemented temporary alert suppressions and adjusted dedup windows.
- 2025-02-13 03:10 UTC — backfill complete, alerts auto-resolved as window passed.

Root cause analysis (hypotheses validated):
1) Upstream ETL/aggregator produced duplicate files during retry logic (S3 object keys contained retry suffix; consumer did not dedupe correctly).
2) Consumer re-ingested historical samples with original timestamps rather than converting to ingestion-time, so Prometheus/remote-write stores treated them as valid, triggering evaluations for past windows.
3) Alerting engine (Grafana) evaluated rules over event-time windows and fired when those past timestamps satisfied thresholds, producing pagers as if the events just happened.
4) High cardinality of a new tag (deployment_id) in backfilled batches created many alerting series and multiplied pages.

Immediate mitigations applied during incident:
- Temporarily increased alert dedup window for noisy latency/error alerts to 30m.
- Enabled a manual mute for the top 12 noisy alert rules for 60 minutes while we validated ingested sample provenance.
- Restarted the ingestion consumer with a consumer flag to squash duplicates by object-id (short-term hotfix).
- Notified dependent teams and suspended automated canary rollbacks that were triggered by those alerts.

Why these mitigations helped (but are not enough):
- Mutes stopped the immediate paging storm but also reduced signal; we temporarily masked potential real regressions.
- Consumer flag is a band-aid — it prevents duplication by object-id but doesn't protect against future replays with different object keys or late-arriving legitimate events.

Proposed durable fixes (prioritized):
1) Producer-side: make ETL job idempotent and emit a unique, deterministic event-id (hash of upstream file + timestamp + source) into each metric sample as label 'ingest_event_id'. Owner: Priya. ETA: 3 sprints.
2) Ingest-time watermarking: record 'ingest_time' as a special label/field and provide an ingest_time-based filter in the remote-write pipeline to optionally ignore samples older than X minutes for alerting-sensitive metrics. Owner: Marcus. ETA: 4 sprints.
3) Alerting policy change: switch critical SLO-related rules to use ingestion-time windowing OR require a minimum 'freshness' (e.g., max(time() - ingest_time) < 120s) before firing. Owner: eng-sre. ETA: 2 sprints.
4) Dedup index in ingestion layer: maintain a short-lived dedupe cache keyed by event-id and object-id for all backfill consumers to reject replays within 48h. Owner: infrastructure team. ETA: 5 sprints.
5) Cardinality guardrails: block new high-cardinality tags via CI check in onboarding pipeline; enforce tag-white-list for aggregated metrics. Owner: metrics-platform. ETA: 3 sprints.
6) Backfill runbook & deploy checklist: require a 'backfill-preview' dashboard and a scheduled mute plan before large backfills. Owner: eng-sre + data-platform. ETA: 1 sprint.

Runbook draft: triage for suspected metric backfill/pager storms
(quick checklist for first responder)
1) Verify customer impact: check APM traces, customer tickets, error budgets. If customers not impacted, treat as suspected telemetry event and escalate to eng-sre.
2) Confirm ingestion lag/backfill: open Grafana dashboard 'Ingest Lag & Replays' (linked) and check ingest_consumer_backfill_rate, remote_write_replay_count.
3) Inspect sample timestamps: query the offending metric with topk to see recent series and inspect timestamps. Example PromQL: 
   - topk(50, increase(request_latency_count[5m]))
   - label_replace(topk(50, increase(request_errors_total[5m])), "ingest_time", "$1", "ingest_time", "(.*)")
4) Correlate with upstream jobs: check ETL job logs for failure/retry windows and object-ids.
5) Apply temporary mitigations: increase dedup window, apply a mute to noisy rules (document who authorized), suspend automated actions triggered by alerts (deploy rollbacks).
6) If ingestion source is trustworthy, coordinate a controlled re-ingest with proper dedupe; if not, stop pipeline and re-evaluate.
7) Post-incident: capture object-ids and sample counts; add to incident ticket and notify teams.

Useful PromQL patterns and notes (examples to add to runbook):
- Find series with timestamps older than X minutes (pseudo-query pattern):
  count_over_time((timestamp(metric_name) < (time() - 3600))[1h:1m])
  (note: PromQL doesn't allow direct timestamp comparison easily; we rely on ingestion_time label where available)

- Recommended alert rule pattern to require freshness: 
  
  # example: only fire if all samples are recent (ingest_time expressed as unix seconds in label)
  avg_over_time((metric{job="frontend"} unless metric{job="frontend",ingest_time!~""})[5m]) > 0

- Backfill volume estimator (for planning mutes):
  sum(increase(ingest_replay_samples_total[1h])) by (source)

Follow-ups and owners (actionable items):
- Priya: implement deterministic event-id in ETL + update producer CI to fail if event-id missing. (SRE-4312) Due: 2025-03-28.
- Marcus: prototype ingest_time label + ingest-side filter; demo to SRE. Due: 2025-04-11.
- Asha/eng-sre: update alerting runbook to prefer ingest_time filters and add 'backfill-preview' dashboard template. Due: 2025-03-14.
- Metrics-platform: build cardinality preflight checks into metrics onboarding. Due: 2025-04-01.
- Infra: short-term dedupe cache for consumers (48h TTL). Due: 2025-05-01.

Lessons learned / heuristics to add to team practice:
- Assume late-arriving samples will always exist: design alerts to prefer freshness checks rather than raw event-time only.
- Mute-before-backfill policy: any planned replays/backfills >100k samples must have scheduled mutes, a draft mitigation plan, and SRE sign-off.
- Surface a single cross-team dashboard for backfill previews: show expected sample volumes by series and cardinality impact.
- Alert burn vs customer impact: add a small automated step to check customer-facing signals (APM, error pages) before firing high-severity pages when metric freshness is ambiguous.

Notes to self (informal):
- We were lucky the real regression was unrelated and short-lived; noise could have killed signal longer.
- Need better observability into the ingestion pipeline — per-object metrics for object_id and replay_count would have saved ~30m.
- Watch out for onboarding PRs that add tags like deployment_id without cardinality review.

Appendix: raw incident artifacts to attach to ticket SRE-4312:
- consumer logs: s3://redwood-logs/ingest-consumer/2025-02-13-backfill.log
- sample counts CSV: /tmp/backfill-sample-counts-2025-02-13.csv
- Grafana dashboard snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d-solo/metrics/ingest-lag?panelId=7&orgId=1

If you find anything missing or have a better containment idea, add as comments below.

-- Asha
